_what: The GRIGOLETTO prompt kit (82 prompts) measured against site-factory's 43 block types.
_why: Task #34 is "give every block type its own prompt". An 82-prompt corpus arrived. Before writing 43 prompts it is worth knowing what this one already answers - and the answer turns out to be that it is organised on a DIFFERENT AXIS, which is more useful than a gap list.

the_finding.claim: THE CORPUS VARIES BY SITE GENRE; THE LIBRARY VARIES BY SECTION. They are not the same list at different resolutions - they are two different axes over the same space.
the_finding.evidence: The 40 site prompts are grouped under 8 genre headings (1. SaaS / Digital Product, 2. Portfolio / Personal Brand, 3. Launch / Product Drop, 4. Agency / Studio, ...), each prompt describing a WHOLE PAGE or a whole hero for that genre. site-factory's 43 types are SECTIONS, reusable across every genre. So a prompt is a column and a block is a row, and neither is a finer version of the other.
the_finding.consequence: The 43 prompts task #34 asks for is not this corpus reorganised. What this corpus supplies is the STYLE half - the cinematic DNA, the stack line, the reduced-motion clause, the "swappable placeholder assets" instruction - which is genre-independent and belongs in every one of the 43. What it cannot supply is the CONTRACT half: what a pricing block requires, which states it must carry, what its accessible name comes from. That is the register's job and always was.

coverage._the_shape_of_the_gap: The 27 unnamed types are almost entirely APPLICATION primitives - checkbox, radio, switch, toast, tooltip, pagination, inspector, masterdetail, objectview, formfield, emptystate, facetstrip, segmentedcontrol, progressbar, progresssteps. The corpus is a MARKETING SITE kit and never claims otherwise, so this is not a shortfall in it. It is the same split found three times already in this programme: the marketing half of the library varies by arrangement and the application half varies by STATE, and no marketing-prompt corpus will ever reach the second.

matcher._what: A keyword match over each prompt's text and title. Not semantic, and hand-checked in both directions rather than trusted.
corrections_made: notificationbadge was matched on "badge" and scored 4. Every one was a MARKETING badge - App Store and Google Play badges, a savings badge, a "Limited drop" badge - and not one was the component. The keyword was narrowed to "notification badge"/"unread count" and the type moved to the unnamed list. A word that matches but never means the thing is a false-positive generator.
team was matched on "team member"/"team grid" and scored 0, while prompt 4.2 (Full agency site) asks for a "team/manifesto" section. The keyword was widened and the type moved to the named list.
matcher._limit: Both errors were found by reading the hits, not by the instrument. There are 40 prompts and 43 types, so a full hand-check is feasible and was only done for the two suspicious counts. Treat the middle of this table as approximate and the two ends as checked.

what_to_take: The Style block, verbatim as a pattern: a fixed DNA line (dark/near-black, dramatic light, depth and parallax, giant serif, film grain) held constant across all 40 so the genre changes and the look does not. That is the same discipline as a token set, expressed as prose to a generator.
The reduced-motion clause and "swappable placeholder assets", which appear in the full-page prompts and are the two instructions that make generated output maintainable rather than a demo.
The three levels of tuning and the five-mistakes list from the Formula section, which is the only part of the kit that teaches rather than supplies.
_what_this_is_not: A judgement of the kit. It does what it says: 82 prompts for cinematic marketing sites, and they are specific and well-built.
A coverage score. 16 of 43 is not a mark out of 43 - the corpus was never aiming at 43 sections.

vendored._why: prompts.json holds all 82 prompts quoted EXACTLY as written. Its digest is vouched so the em-dash gate exempts it: rewriting somebody else's punctuation to suit a house style would make every prompt in this repository a paraphrase of the one they actually shipped.
